pattern.crimePattern: landowner kills the valuer who exposed crops planted to inflate a compensation claim
pattern.notes: Fictional energy company and farm on the rim of a real crater. Planting before a valuation cut-off is a widely reported pattern; no real project, company or person is depicted.

ob.reportedBy: Sammy Rono, gate attendant, Menengai crater viewpoint
ob.text: The gate attendant at the Menengai crater viewpoint reports that a visitor found a woman on a ledge about 40 m below the viewpoint wall at 18:10. She is identified as Beryl Adoyo (33), a valuation surveyor. Her company car is parked inside the gate.

people.name: Beryl Adoyo
people.occupation: Valuation surveyor, Rift Steam Energy pipeline
people.bio: Values crops and trees on farms along a new steam pipeline, so landowners can be paid compensation. Known for re-measuring everything twice.

image.brief: Kenyan woman, early 30s, short braids tied back, a company fleece with a small pipeline logo in plain shapes, a measuring tape clipped to her belt, a camera strap around her neck, focused and friendly, ID-photo framing

people.name: Kimaiyo Rotich
people.bio: Farms twelve acres on the crater edge. His compensation claim was cut from KSh 4.2 million to 0.6 million last week.

image.brief: Kenyan Kalenjin man, early 60s, lean and weathered, a hand-knitted green wool sweater with a thick rolled collar, a walking stick, a felt hat in his hand, stern and proud, ID-photo framing

people.name: Duncan Kibe
people.bio: Beryl's colleague. Sent her an angry email that morning about the project timeline.

image.brief: Kenyan man, mid 30s, orange hard hat under his arm, company overalls with a reflective strip, safety glasses pushed up, defensive, ID-photo framing

people.name: Philemon Kiptoo
people.bio: Runs the farm day to day: the cows, the milking, the planting.

image.brief: Kenyan man, about 40, gumboots, a worn work jacket over a shirt, a milk can at his feet, uneasy, ID-photo framing

people.name: Sammy Rono
people.bio: Runs the gate on the crater rim road: tickets, the visitors' book, a radio.

people.name: Ivy Njenga
people.bio: Came up for the sunset. Found Beryl's clipboard on the path and looked over the wall.

people.name: Chepkoech Langat
people.bio: Milks on the Rotich farm morning and evening.

locations.name: Menengai crater viewpoint
locations.description: The rim of a huge crater. Far below, steam plumes rise from geothermal well pads. A low stone wall, waist-high, runs along the viewpoint. A clipboard lies on the path. Beryl's company car is parked 200 m back, inside the gate.

hotspots.label: Over the wall
hotspots.text: Forty metres down, on a ledge, the rangers have reached her. They bring up what they can.

hotspots.label: Her camera (recovered)
hotspots.text: The rangers bring up her camera with the strap still on. The screen is cracked but it works.

hotspots.label: Clipboard on the path
hotspots.text: Her clipboard, face down on the path, a pen still clipped to it. The wall here is waist-high.

hotspots.label: Her company car
hotspots.text: Her car, unlocked. On the passenger seat, a valuation file with a red tab: ROTICH.

hotspots.label: Glovebox
hotspots.text: In the glovebox, folded small, a handwritten letter.

hotspots.label: Her phone, on the dashboard
hotspots.text: Her phone is on the dashboard, unlocked by her brother on the phone from Kisumu. The last email she opened is angry.

hotspots.label: Back seat
hotspots.text: A box of wayleave agreements for the pipeline route, filed by farm.

hotspots.label: Gate hut
hotspots.text: The gate hut. Every car that comes up the rim road is written in the visitors' book with its plate.

hotspots.label: Gate attendant
hotspots.text: Sammy Rono stands at the gate with his radio, looking at the wall and not at anything else.

hotspots.label: The visitor
hotspots.text: Ivy Njenga sits on the wall with her back to the crater.

image.brief: the rim of Menengai crater near Nakuru in late afternoon light, a low stone wall at a viewpoint, the vast caldera below with white geothermal steam plumes rising from well pads on its floor, a dirt path along the rim, no people in focus

locations.name: The Rotich farm, crater edge
locations.description: Twelve acres on the crater edge. A strip along the pipeline route is planted with rows of avocado seedlings and a line of young eucalyptus, the soil around each one still loose.

hotspots.label: The pipeline strip
hotspots.text: Nine hundred seedlings in fresh rings of turned soil, every one the same height. Nothing else on the farm was planted this year.

image.brief: a small farm on the edge of a crater in the Kenyan highlands, a strip of freshly planted avocado seedlings in neat rows of turned red soil, young eucalyptus, a cattle shed and milk cans in the background

locations.name: Rift Steam well pad, crater floor
locations.description: A fenced well pad on the crater floor: a drilling rig, a site office in a container, a shift board.

hotspots.label: Shift board
hotspots.text: The shift log: every engineer signs every hour, a safety rule.

image.brief: a geothermal drilling pad on the floor of a crater, a drilling rig, steam venting, a site office made from a shipping container, a fenced compound

facts.text: Beryl Adoyo was found on a ledge about 40 m below the Menengai viewpoint wall at 18:10.
Recovered from the ledge with her camera strap still around her neck.
In her pocket: a Rift Steam canteen receipt for lunch at 12:45.
The viewpoint wall is waist-high. Her clipboard lay face down on the path beside it.
Her last photos, 16:18–16:24, show the Rotich strip from above: rows of fresh planting rings.
Her last frame, 16:24: a small figure in a green sweater coming up the path behind her.
Valuation file, Rotich farm: seedlings planted about 14 days before the cut-off date. Claim cut from KSh 4.2 million to 0.6 million.
Kimaiyo's handwritten letter to Beryl: 'You will regret this.'
Wayleave agreement: Kimaiyo signed his consent to the pipeline route two years ago.
Visitors' book: Beryl's company car in at 15:58.
Visitors' book: 'KCA 7xxX — K. Rotich — in 16:12, out 16:48.'
Visitors' book: 'I. Njenga — in 17:55.'
Sammy: at about 16:20 an older man in a green sweater walked up the path towards the viewpoint.
Sammy: at about 16:45 the same man walked fast back to his car and drove off.
Sammy was at the gate all afternoon; every entry in the visitors' book is in his hand.
Ivy: she arrived about 18:00, saw a clipboard on the path, looked over the wall and called the gate.
Kimaiyo Rotich wears a hand-knitted green wool sweater. He refuses to hand it over.
Seized from Kimaiyo in detention: his hand-knitted green wool sweater, hand-spun yarn.
Well-pad shift log: D. Kibe signed every hour from 14:00 to 18:00 on the crater floor.
Duncan's email to Beryl that morning: 'Your valuations are holding up the whole schedule.'
Duncan: valuers never handle money. Compensation is paid by the finance office after the valuation is signed.
Chepkoech: Philemon supervised the evening milking with them from 16:00 to 18:30.
Philemon: Mzee told them to plant the seedlings at night, two weeks before the cut-off. "I said it was wrong."
Philemon: Mzee had never met Beryl before the valuation. "No family, no history. Just the valuation."
Autopsy: injuries consistent with a fall from height.
Autopsy: fingertip bruises on both upper arms, made shortly before death, as if gripped hard from the front.
Autopsy: no blow to the head before the fall; no vehicle injuries.
Autopsy: death between 15:30 and 17:30; stomach contents three to four hours after the 12:45 lunch narrow it to about 16:00–17:00.
Autopsy: green wool fibres under her fingernails, kept for comparison.
Lab: the green hand-spun wool under her fingernails matches Kimaiyo's sweater.
Toxicology: clean. No drugs, no alcohol, no poison.
Kimaiyo: "I haven't been up to the crater in years. I was on my farm all afternoon."
Kimaiyo: "That girl cheated me."
Kimaiyo admits he drove up after her and spoke to her at the viewpoint. He says she was standing at the wall when he left.
Kimaiyo: "I never touched her. She was standing there when I left."
Kimaiyo, shown the fibre result, admits he took her by the arms "to make her listen".
Duncan: "I was on the pad all afternoon. The email was about drilling delays."
Philemon: "I was milking with the workers."

interrogations.intro: Kimaiyo stands at his farm gate with his stick planted in the red soil. "That valuer. Yes. She cheated me. I have nothing else to say."

topics.reply: Those trees are mine. I planted them on my land. What does it matter when?
I wrote what I felt. Old men are allowed to write letters.

interrogations.intro: Duncan takes his hard hat off and holds it in both hands. "I sent her an angry email this morning. I'll never be able to take it back."

topics.reply: She was the only honest valuer we had. That's why she was slow.
Valuers never handle money. Finance pays after she signs. She signed what she saw, and she saw everything.

interrogations.intro: Philemon keeps working the pump handle of the milk cooler. "I manage cows. I don't manage Mzee."

topics.reply: Mzee told us to plant them at night. Two weeks before the date. I said it was wrong. He said, "It's my land."
He had never met her before the valuation. No family, no history. Only that paper.
Ask Chepkoech. She milks beside me every evening.

interrogations.intro: Sammy keeps one hand on his radio. "I write every car. Every one. That's my job."

topics.reply: Mzee Rotich? Yes, he came up at twelve past four. An old man in a green sweater walked up to the viewpoint after that. Then he came back fast and drove away.

interrogations.intro: Ivy can't stop rubbing her arms, though it isn't cold. "I came for the sunset."

topics.reply: The clipboard was just lying there. Nobody leaves a clipboard. So I looked.

contradictions.reaction: I went up to talk to her. Only talk. I asked her to look again at my trees. She laughed. I came down. She was standing there when I left.
A long silence. "...I took her arms. To make her listen. Thirty years on that land. She laughed at me." He says nothing else.

words.text: struck on the head and thrown over
her valuation exposed the crops he'd planted just before the deadline
a dispute over the pipeline route through his farm

prosecutor.pass: The gate book puts him on the rim, and his own sweater is under her nails. That will hold.
fail: Doesn't hold up. An angry email from the crater floor isn't a man on the rim. Who walked up that path at twenty past four?
No. Read the gate book against what he told you.

prosecutor.pass: Gripped by both arms from the front, no blow first. Pushed. Yes.
fail: The pathologist disagrees with you. Read what she found on the arms, and what she didn't find on the head.
An accident doesn't leave fingertip bruises. Try again.

prosecutor.pass: Nine hundred seedlings planted at night. That's the reason, and the court will understand it.
fail: He signed the route two years ago. That isn't it.
Who gains, and from what paper? Look at the valuation.

proof.concludes: Kimaiyo said he hadn't been up to the crater in years, but the gate book has him in at 16:12 and out at 16:48, and Sammy saw a man in green walk up at 16:20 and back at 16:45. He admits confronting her.
She died about 16:00–17:00, gripped hard by both arms from the front just before the fall, with no blow first. Her last photo shows a figure in a green sweater coming up the path at 16:24.
The wool under her nails is from Kimaiyo's sweater. She was photographing his night-planted strip from above. Kimaiyo Rotich pushed Beryl from the crater rim because her valuation exposed his crops.

eliminations.why: Duncan signed the shift log on the crater floor every hour from 14:00 to 18:00.
Philemon was supervising the evening milking with the workers from 16:00 to 18:30.
Sammy was at the gate all afternoon; every entry in the book is in his hand.
Ivy only came through the gate at 17:55.
There was no blow to the head before the fall.
An accident doesn't leave grip bruises on both arms, and her last frame shows someone coming up behind her.
No vehicle injuries, and her car was parked 200 m back inside the gate.
He signed his consent to the route two years ago.
That was Duncan's anger, and Duncan was on the crater floor.
He had never met her before the valuation.
Valuers never handle money; nothing passed between them.

reconstruction.text: Two weeks before the cut-off date, Kimaiyo has 900 seedlings and a row of eucalyptus planted at night on the pipeline strip.
Beryl's valuation sees the fresh rings. The claim drops from KSh 4.2 million to 0.6 million. He writes: "You will regret this."
15:58. She drives up to the rim to photograph the strip from above, where the rings show clearly. At 16:12 his car follows her through the gate.
16:24. Her last frame catches a man in green on the path. At the wall he grips her by both arms. She pushes back at the wool of his sweater.
16:48. He drives out past the gate. Below the wall, her clipboard lies face down on the path.

clockPlan.note: Detain after the gate book breaks his claim; fibres take 12 h; press inside the 24 hours. No rush.

tier1.line: Every car on the rim road is in a book at the gate. Read it against what the old man told you.

tier2.line: Her last photo shows someone in green. Look at what he wears, and think about what a lab could do with it.

tier1.line: Dr. Chebii found bruises before she found anything else. Where are they?

tier2.line: Gripped from the front by both arms, and no blow to the head first. Say what that is.

tier1.line: Read her file on his farm. Then look at what she was photographing.

tier2.line: Fresh planting rings, two weeks before the deadline. Who loses three and a half million?

glossary.def: Respectful word for an older man.

tutorial.line: New tools, Detective. A pathologist, a lab, and a clock. Detaining someone gives you 24 hours. Use them, don't waste them.
Dr. Chebii doesn't guess. Read what she found, and also what she didn't.
The clock is running. Take what you need from him, send it to the lab, and keep working while it cooks.

ui.beatNotes: The autopsy report, the lab queue and the arrest clock, all at once. Dr. Chebii delivers the autopsy as a short dry voice-note plus the written report; the lab queue is a clipboard on the corkboard with ticking tags; detaining someone puts a red 24-hour clock on their photo. The charge sheet gains HOW.
